e: Coined in an early text-based computer game, Hunt the Wumpus (published 1973).
q: In addition to the Wumpus, other dangers are lurking: namely deadly pits, and bats that grab the player and drop her in a random cave.
1987, Etienne Wenger, Artificial Intelligence and Tutoring Systems:
A scream occurs when the agent shoots an arrow that kills the wumpus.
2003, Selmer Bringsjord, Michael John Zenzen, Superminds: People Harness Hypercomputation, and More:
In Hunter, towards the end of the game, the player is tracking the wounded wumpus and finds herself in a room of interconnected caves.

e: Borrowed from Ulster Scots wumman, from Middle English womman.
q: For I'll hif to get a wumman, or the place'll suffer loss

e: From the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of the Mandarin pronunciation of Chinese 五毛 (wǔmáo), a clipping of 五毛黨 /五毛党 (wǔmáodǎng, literally “the 5 dime party”), in reference to allegations that the Chinese government employs online shills paid 1/2 yuan RMB per online post.
